Ratings are for targeting each fish inshore in Pinellas, from FWC science and local reports. Harvest closures are FWC's. Water temperature: NOAA Clearwater Beach monthly average.

winterSnook pull back to warm, low-salinity water: residential canals, deep creeks, dark-bottom bayous and the backs of marinas. Fish the warmest part of the afternoon, slowly. Mornings are best in deep canals and creek mouths. Afternoons are best on sunny, muddy shorelines.
springAs the water passes about 70°F, fish leave the canals for creek and canal mouths, then the outer mangrove islands and docks along the flats. Whitebait arrive, and so does the best fishing of the year. March and April are open for harvest.
summerSnook move to the passes and beaches to spawn. Johns Pass and Clearwater Pass are documented spawning sites. Sight-fish the beach troughs at dawn, and fish the passes and jetties on the tide changes. Harvest is closed; handle fish gently in the heat.
fall · nowFish come off the beaches to outside mangroves, rocks, points and docks, then up into the creeks as the water cools. Bait is everywhere. September through November is open for harvest.

Bait and lures

Livewhitebait, threadfin, pinfish, pigfish, mojarra, finger mullet, shrimp, small blue crabs
Cutladyfish chunks, cut mullet (mostly bigger fish around passes)
Luresjerkbaits, paddletail swimbaits, topwater walkers at dawn, flair hawk jigs at night, DOA shrimp around dock lights
Free-lineKnocker rigJighead and soft plastic

How to fish it

  • Snook are ambush feeders that won't chase far. Put the bait right on the edge of cover and let the current bring it in.
  • Snook gill plates cut line. Use 30–40 lb fluorocarbon leader; go heavier at bridges.
  • Lighted docks and bridges at night, on a moving tide, are the classic pattern.
  • At the passes, outgoing water carries bait to fish holding behind the rocks.

At your spots

Dock: Lighted docks along the Intracoastal hold snook from spring through fall, best at night and on dawn falling tides.
Clearwater: A documented spawning site. Summer fish stack along the jetty rocks; fall fish hold on the bridge.
Johns Pass: A documented spawning site. Fish the jetty and bridge fenders on the outgoing tide.

Worth knowing

  • They spawn from April/May to September/October, peaking June–July, in late afternoon and evening. Spawning schools of 400–500 come back to the same pass every year.research
  • They're born male and many change to female after a spawn. Half of females are mature at about 30", which is why the slot tops out at 33".research
  • Cold kills snook. They go sluggish below 65°F and start dying around 50°F, faster when the drop is sudden.research
IDA black lateral line runs all the way into the tail. Sloped forehead, a jutting lower jaw, a yellowish pelvic fin.

winterVery low winter tides (below zero on the tide table) push reds out of the shallows into troughs, sand holes and deep dock lines next to flats that go dry. The water is clear, so it's sight-fishing weather, and tailing fish show up on sunny afternoons. They often mix with sheepshead on docks.
springFish that wintered in canals and bayous come back out to the mouths and onto the flats. Schools push mullet across the grass on the high tide.
summerLook in potholes on the flats early. High tides push reds deep under flooded mangroves, so skip a cut bait right into the roots. As the tide falls they move back to the mangrove edges and oyster bars.
fall · nowThe best months. Reds work down-bay toward the Gulf and feed hard at creek and canal mouths. From late August to November, big breeder schools (mostly females over 30") gather around the passes and the Egmont Key drop-offs to spawn.

Bait and lures

Livewhitebait, pinfish, shrimp, fiddler crabs, finger mullet
Cutcut pinfish, cut ladyfish, cut mullet, cut threadfin, half a blue crab
Luresgold weedless spoon, paddletail on a light jighead, weedless jerkbait, topwater on calm mornings
Carolina / fish-finder rigPopping corkJighead and soft plasticFree-line

How to fish it

  • A cut bait sitting on the bottom at the edge of a pothole or mangrove point is the most reliable redfish rig in Pinellas.
  • Come in quietly by drifting, poling or with the trolling motor. Pinellas reds that get spooked don't settle back down.
  • Give a spot about five minutes, then move. Dolphins push fish around.
  • Bites are best on the incoming and the first part of the outgoing. On the falling tide, fish the first deep water the fish drop back to.
  • Use 20–30 lb fluorocarbon leader by water clarity, and check it often around oysters.

At your spots

Dock: Winter reds hold on dock pilings and seawall corners, especially on low tides. Try cut bait or shrimp on the bottom.
Clearwater: Fall breeders pass through. Slot fish are on the bay-side flats and around the spoil islands.
Johns Pass: Boca Ciega Bay just inside is classic redfish water, especially the bayous and the flats toward Pass-a-Grille.

Worth knowing

  • Adults spawn nearshore from late August to November. Tampa Bay fish spawn earlier than Charlotte Harbor fish.research
  • Fish over the slot are the breeders. Keep them in the water, and release them fast.research
IDOne or more black spots near the tail. Copper-bronze color, and a down-turned mouth for bottom feeding.

winterTrout move into deep holes, canals, channel edges and dark mud and shell bottoms that warm up on sunny afternoons. The murky green holes near Fort De Soto, Bunces Pass and the Bulkhead are known winter spots. Dock and bridge lights hold fish at night.
springBy about mid-April they move out onto the grass flats, sometimes in under a yard of water. The spawn starts in April, and big females hold on island edges over grass and sand.
summerFish the deeper grass edges (4–6 ft) at first light, then deeper water as it heats up. Topwater at dawn is how the big "gator" trout get caught.
fall · nowThe best trout fishing of the year. Fish spread across the flats and potholes, and they eat almost anything under a cork.

Bait and lures

Liveshrimp, whitebait, pigfish, pinfish
Luressoft plastic shrimp or paddletail on a 1/8–1/4 oz jighead, suspending twitchbait, topwater walker at dawn
Popping corkJighead and soft plasticFree-line

How to fish it

  • Drift the flats and cast ahead of the boat. When you catch one, work the area, because trout school by size.
  • A shrimp or whitebait under a popping cork over 3–5 ft of grass is the go-to.
  • Drop to 15–20 lb fluorocarbon in clear winter water.
  • Trout have soft mouths. Use a loose drag, and don't horse them.

At your spots

Dock: Lighted docks hold trout at night in the cool months, along with snook.
Clearwater: The grass flats behind Sand Key and Clearwater Harbor are reliable in spring and fall.
Johns Pass: The Boca Ciega Bay grass flats inside the pass.

Worth knowing

  • The Gulf spawn peaks April–July. Males drum audibly on spawning sites, and FWC has mapped Tampa Bay's.research
  • Trout move deep in the hottest and coldest months.FWC
IDRound black spots on the back, the dorsal fin and the tail. Two prominent canine teeth in the upper jaw.

winterMostly gone. A few fish stay in deep backwater canals and the Skyway area. Don't plan around them.
springThe first fish roll near the Skyway in late March in warm years. By May, schools are moving along the beaches inside about a mile, and the run is on.
summerPeak season. Look for beach schools at dawn off the Pinellas beaches and Egmont Key. In the passes, the hard outgoing tides around new and full moons flush pass crabs out, and tarpon line up to eat them (the "crab flush"). At night, fish the bridge lights and the Skyway with threadfins.
fall · nowFewer fish, scattered on bay reefs, channels and backwater ponds. Rolling pods show up on the St. Pete reef. Juvenile tarpon stay in the mangrove ponds.

Bait and lures

Livethreadfin (dollar-size), pass crabs, pinfish, mullet, large whitebait
Cutcut mullet or threadfin on the bottom in the passes
Lures5–7" soft swimbaits, DOA Baitbuster, large jigs in the passes
Free-lineTarpon float rig

How to fish it

  • Use a 5/0–8/0 circle hook, 60–80 lb fluoro leader and 30–50 lb braid. A hooked fish shouldn't get a long fight.
  • Bow to the fish when it jumps (push the rod tip toward it) so a jump doesn't break the line.
  • Watch for sharks after long fights in summer. Break the fish off if a shark is on it.
  • Crab flush: the strong evening outgoing tides 2–3 days either side of a May–July new or full moon.

At your spots

Dock: Juvenile and mid-size tarpon cruise the Intracoastal under the lights in summer.
Clearwater: The bridge and the pass at night, plus crab flushes on strong evening outgoing tides.
Johns Pass: A crab flush pass in summer. Fish on the bridge lights at night.

Worth knowing

  • Tarpon spawn offshore. The leptocephalus larvae drift into mangrove ponds and grow there for years.research
  • They can gulp air, so they can live in stagnant backwater ponds.research
IDBig silver scales, an upturned mouth, and a long filament on the last dorsal ray.

winterPrime time. Big fish move into the bay and onto every piling, dock and jetty with barnacles. The spawn peaks late February into March, depending on the water temperature.
springIn March and April spawning fish gather on nearshore reefs, rock piles and markers, and the bay bite thins out by May.
summerSmaller fish stay on docks and seawalls. It's not worth targeting them.
fall · nowFish come back onto bay structure in November as the water cools.

Bait and lures

Livefiddler crabs, shrimp, sand fleas
Cutoyster, clam, a piece of shrimp, barnacles scraped off the piling as chum
Luressmall jighead tipped with shrimp
Knocker rigJighead and soft plastic

How to fish it

  • Fish straight down along the piling, not out in the current.
  • The bite feels like a light tap. Set the hook short and sharp, before the fish strips the bait.
  • Use a strong 1/0 hook on 15–20 lb fluorocarbon.
  • They bite best early and late in the tide flow, when the current is slower.
  • Scraping barnacles off the piling starts a feeding frenzy.

At your spots

Dock: The dock's best winter fish. Fish the pilings with fiddlers or shrimp on a knocker rig, especially in slack and slow water.
Clearwater: The jetty rocks and bridge fenders from December to March.
Johns Pass: The bridge fenders and jetty from December to March. Fish them on the slower parts of the tide.

Worth knowing

  • They spawn on nearshore rocks, reefs and markers in late winter and early spring, which is why FWC caps boats at 50 in March and April.FWC
  • Human-like teeth crush barnacles, oysters and crabs.research
ID5–7 black vertical bars, and human-like teeth.

winterFish gather to spawn from January through April, peaking around March. Schools of an acre or more can show in 10–14 ft of water in the bay.
springThey follow the bar edges up-bay to the Gandy, Howard Frankland and Courtney Campbell bridges, and many stay there through summer.
summerBridge and dock fish. They're always on the down-current side of the pilings.
fall · nowBig fish leave the bridges. Smaller drum mix with reds and sheepshead on docks.

Bait and lures

Liveshrimp, fiddler crabs
Cuthalf a blue crab (shell on), clams
Carolina / fish-finder rigKnocker rig

How to fish it

  • Put the bait on the bottom just down-current of the piling.
  • Big drum (over 30") are spawners with wormy, tough meat. Release them.

At your spots

Dock: Small drum hold around the dock pilings in winter alongside sheepshead.
Clearwater: Fish the bridge and jetties in late winter.
Johns Pass: Fish the bridge and jetties in late winter.

Worth knowing

  • They spawn nearshore in winter and early spring. Males drum loud enough to hear through a hull.FWC

How to fish it

  • Look for sand just down-tide of structure: docks, pier ends, bridge pilings and the edges of the passes.
  • Drag the bait slowly. When you feel the thump, wait a few seconds before setting the hook.

Dock: Sandy bottom around the dock in spring and summer.
Clearwater: Sand edges along the jetties in fall, catch and release from Oct 15.
Johns Pass: Sand edges along the jetties in fall, catch and release from Oct 15.

Worth knowing

  • Gulf flounder have three eyespots in a triangle. Southern flounder have none. Both count toward the same limit.research
  • Fall run timing comes from Gulf-wide sources. There isn't a Tampa Bay–specific study.local reports

winterBigger fish move to nearshore reefs and wrecks. The bay has small fish only.
springFish start showing on bay structure in April and May.
summerPeak. Docks, bridge pilings, seawalls, rock piles in 6–10 ft and bay artificial reefs. Chum with whitebait to start them biting.
fall · nowStill good on bay structure through October, then the bigger fish move out.

Bait and lures

Liveshrimp, small whitebait, small pinfish
Cutcut whitebait, cut threadfin

How to fish it

  • They're leader-shy. Use 15–20 lb fluorocarbon and the smallest circle hook that holds the bait.
  • Chum a few live whitebait (or crushed ones) over the structure, then drift a bait back with them.

At your spots

Dock: A summer staple on the dock pilings and seawall. Expect lots of shorts. Keepers are 10"+.
Clearwater: Fish the jetty rocks and bridge in summer.
Johns Pass: Fish the jetty rocks and bridge in summer.

Worth knowing

  • Juveniles grow up in the bay and mangroves, and adults move offshore to spawn in summer.research

How to fish it

  • Look for diving birds and bait spraying on the surface.
  • Retrieve fast. Use a 30–40 lb fluorocarbon bite leader or light wire, and no shiny swivels (macks hit them).
  • Chumming with whitebait brings them to the boat.

At your spots

Dock: Occasional in the Intracoastal in spring and fall.
Clearwater: Fish the mouth of the pass and the beach in spring and fall.

Rules people get wrong

FWC manages snook, redfish and trout by region. Almost all of Pinellas is in the Tampa Bay Region, which runs from Fred Howard Park south to SR 64 in Manatee County. The Anclote River and the waters around it belong to the Big Bend Region instead, where the trout bag is 5 rather than 3.

License
Florida residents can get a free resident shoreline license for fishing from land or a dock attached to land. It doesn't cover a boat. The resident annual saltwater license is $17. Under 16 and residents 65+ are exempt.
Snook permit
$10/yr ($50 for five years, residents only). Needed to keep a snook, even with the shoreline license.
No trebles with bait
No multiple hooks with live or dead natural bait for snook, reds, trout, sheepshead, black drum, flounder or tarpon. Lures with trebles are fine.
Reef fish gear
For gray snapper and grouper: a circle hook with natural bait, a dehooking device, and a descending device or venting tool rigged and ready.
State Reef Fish Survey
Free, and needed on a private boat to keep gag, red grouper, red snapper, amberjack, hogfish, triggerfish and some others (not mangrove snapper).
Tarpon
Fish over 40" stay in the water.
Sharks from shore
Anglers 16+ need the free Shore-based Shark permit. Circle hooks and a cutting tool are required, and chumming from the beach isn't allowed.
Pinellas mullet
Oct 1–Jan 31: 5 striped mullet per person and per boat in the northeast St. Pete bayous (Riviera, Bayou Grande, Smack's, Snell Isle, Coffee Pot).
Unregulated species
Ladyfish, jacks, whiting, pinfish: 2 fish or 100 lb per person per day, whichever is more.

Rules change, sometimes mid-season after red tide or a cold kill. Before you keep a fish, confirm the rule at myfwc.com or in the Fish Rules app.

Rigs

Free-line

BuildMain line → double uni → 2–3 ft fluorocarbon leader → circle hook. No weight.
Hooks1/0–3/0 circle for whitebait, 4/0–8/0 for threadfin and tarpon baits.
UseLive bait drifting naturally into cover or down a current line.
LegalCircle hooks are required for sharks and reef fish with natural bait.

Popping cork

BuildMain line → clacker cork → 2–3 ft fluorocarbon → 1/0 circle hook or a 1/8 oz jighead.
Hooks1/0 circle
UseShrimp or whitebait over 3–6 ft of grass for trout, reds and tripletail. Pop it every few seconds.

Knocker rig

BuildA small egg sinker sliding on the leader, stopped right against the hook eye.
Hooks1/0 J or circle for sheepshead; up to 3/0 for snook in current.
UseTight to pilings, jetties and dock posts. The bait stays put, and you feel every tap.

Carolina / fish-finder rig

BuildEgg sinker → bead → swivel → 18–30" leader → circle hook.
Hooks1/0–5/0 circle
UseCut bait or crab on the bottom for reds and black drum. Mud minnows for flounder.

Jighead and soft plastic

Build1/8–1/4 oz on the flats, 3/8–1/2 oz in the passes. Paddletail or shrimp tail, or tipped with live shrimp.
UseCovering water for trout, reds, flounder, snook and pompano (a pompano jig).
LegalA single hook. Fine with natural bait.

Pompano (double dropper) rig

BuildA pyramid sinker at the bottom with two dropper loops above it, each with a small float and a #1–1/0 hook.
Hooks#1–1/0
UseSand fleas or shrimp in the surf for pompano and whiting.

Clark spoon trolling rig

BuildA planer or trolling sinker → 15–20 ft of 30 lb fluorocarbon → Clark spoon.
UseSpanish mackerel along the channels and beaches at 5–7 knots.

Deep-diving plug

Build60–80 lb leader to a deep-diving plug.
UseGag in season along the bay's channel edges.

Tarpon float rig

BuildA balloon or cork 4–6 ft above a 60–80 lb leader and a 5/0–8/0 circle hook.
Hooks5/0–8/0 circle
UseCrab or threadfin drifting in the passes and on beach schools.
LegalFish over 40" stay in the water.

Shark rig

BuildWire bite leader (shorter than 4 ft from shore unless you have the shore permit) → non-offset, non-stainless circle hook.
Hooks6/0–12/0 circle
UseCut bait for blacktips and bulls.
LegalShore anglers 16+ need the free shore-based shark permit to target sharks, or to use wire over 4 ft.

Knots

Improved clinch / PalomarLine or leader to a hook or swivel.
Double uni / FGBraid to fluorocarbon leader.
Non-slip loopJerkbaits and jigs, for more action.

What the temperature means

50°F: Snook die in sustained water this cold (lab range 47–51°F). FWC asks anglers to ease off after a cold kill.research
60°F: Snook stop feeding below about 58–60°F. Trout and reds slide into deep holes and canals.research
65°F: Snook turn sluggish and head for canals, creeks and other warm refuges.research
68°F: Cobia, kingfish and Spanish mackerel start running north along the beaches.local reports
72°F: Whitebait push onto the grass flats, and live-bait fishing takes off.local reports

Red tide

Karenia brevis is in the Gulf at low levels all year and blooms most often in fall. Blooms can last months. Fish kills start above about 100,000 cells/L. The briefing already checks FWC's samples within 20 km. FWC can put Tampa Bay snook, reds and trout on catch and release after a bad bloom. Report fish kills to 800-636-0511.FWC

Cold fronts

A hard drop sends snook and trout deep and shuts the bite off for a day or two. The clear water and very low tides after a front are great for sight-fishing reds on the flats. After a cold kill, give snook a break.research

Summer rain

Heavy rain dumps fresh water into the bay and pushes reds and mackerel toward the bay mouth. Dead grass fouls treble hooks, so switch to weedless lures.local reports

Seagrass and hurricanes

Tampa Bay had about 31,500 acres of seagrass in early 2024, up 1,407 acres since 2022, but still short of the 40,000-acre goal, and Old Tampa Bay hit a record low. That mapping came before Helene and Milton, and the post-storm survey (winter 2025–26 imagery) isn't out yet.research
